newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's 96 inflation rises to 15.9 pct-ADB.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's 96 inflation rises to 15.9 pct-ADB.

text.p: Sri Lanka's inflation rate as measured by the consumer price index rose to 15.9 percent in 1996, sharply up from 7.7 percent in the previous year, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said on Thursday.

"The rise in food prices, the higher cost of imports as the currency depreciated, and the interruption to the flow of goods for some parts of the country affected by the fighting were the major contributory factors. Increased power costs and higher wages in some sectors also stoked inflation," the bank's annual report said.
Sri Lanka is fighting a war, now in its 14th year, against Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels who demand a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east.
The ADB report projected inflation would slow to 10 percent in 1997 and eight percent in 1998.

"Pressure on prices is likely to be strong in the first half of 1997 owing to the upward revision of state-administered prices and depreciation of the Sri Lanka rupee. Increases in salaries of civil servants over two years will also exert upward pressure on prices," the report said.
